title: श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता — विभूतियोगः
titleEn: The Bhagavad Gītā — Chapter 10: The Divine Manifestations
draftNote: Prepared by the Lectorium pipeline from the vulgate text, with a drafting pass, a reviewing pass and a mechanical gate; a printed-edition collation and audio are still to come. Use ⚑ correction on any verse to report a problem.
source: Text: the received (vulgate) text of the Bhagavadgītā, Mahābhārata 6.23–40, as read by Śaṅkara's commentary. Devanagari from Sanskrit Wikisource (भगवद्गीता/विभूतियोगः), collated verse by verse against the GRETIL romanized text based on the BORI critical edition (input Tokunaga, rev. J. Smith); every verse where the two differ carries a note giving the BORI reading, and every correction to the Wikisource text is named in its note. Collation against a pre-1930 printed edition is still to be done. Transliteration: IAST. The reading under each word gives the words with sandhi undone and compound members hyphenated, in the manner of the traditional pada-pāṭha. Pronunciation convention: classical Sanskrit as described in Whitney's Sanskrit Grammar (1889); no audio yet. Translations made fresh from the Sanskrit with Monier-Williams (1899), Apte (1890) and Śaṅkara's commentary for the traditional sense; no modern translation consulted.

sentences.t: श्रीभगवानुवाच
sentences.tr: śrībhagavān uvāca
sentences.l: The Blessed Lord said

morph.gloss: holy, glorious (honorific prefix)
the Blessed One, the Lord — Kṛṣṇa's title as speaker (nom. sg. bhagavān; -n + u- written joined)
to speak (uvāca: perfect 3rd sg. 'said')

sentences.t:
भूय एव महाबाहो शृणु मे परमं वचः ।
यत्तेऽहं प्रीयमाणाय वक्ष्यामि हितकाम्यया ॥
sentences.tr:
bhūyaḥ eva mahā-bāho śṛṇu me paramam vacaḥ |
yat te aham prīyamāṇāya vakṣyāmi hita-kāmyayā ||

morph.gloss: again, further, once more (bhūyaḥ: adverb; visarga dropped before the vowel e- of eva, -aḥ + e- → -a e-, the rule for any visarga before a non-a vowel)
indeed, just
great (first compound member)
arm (mahā-bāhu: 'great-armed', an epithet of Arjuna, vocative sg.)
to hear, listen (śṛṇu: imperative 2nd sg. 'listen!')
I (me: gen. sg. enclitic 'my', governing vacaḥ)
supreme, highest (acc. sg. neut., agreeing with vacaḥ)
word, speech (acc. sg. neut., object of śṛṇu)
which (yat: acc. sg. neut. relative, referring back to vacaḥ of pāda a, object of vakṣyāmi; -t + t- → -tt-, assimilation)
you (te: dat. sg. enclitic 'to you', governed with prīyamāṇāya)
I (nom. sg., subject of vakṣyāmi; te + aham: -e + a- → -e with avagraha)
to please, delight (prīyamāṇa: passive present participle 'being pleased, being dear', dat. sg. masc., agreeing with te)
to speak, declare (vakṣyāmi: future 1st sg. 'I shall declare')
benefit, welfare (first compound member)
desire, wish (hita-kāmyā: 'a wish for [your] welfare', instr. sg. fem., adverbial 'out of a desire for your benefit')

sentences.l: Again indeed, O great-armed-one, hear my supreme word — which to-you, dear, I-shall-declare, out-of-a-wish-for-benefit.
sentences.i: Once again, Mahābāho, hear my supreme word, which I will speak to you, so dear to me, for your benefit.
sentences.n: Kṛṣṇa resumes the teaching begun in chapter 9 (bhūyaḥ eva, 'once again'); yat, 'which', looks back to vacaḥ, 'word', already named in pāda a — the very word he is about to speak. Mahābāho, 'great-armed one', addresses Arjuna. Sandhi: भूय is bhūyaḥ with its visarga dropped before the vowel e- of eva (-aḥ + e- → -a e-, the rule for a visarga before any vowel but a-); यत्तेऽहं packs yat+te (-t+t-→-tt-) + aham (avagraha, -e+a-→-e).

sentences.t:
न मे विदुः सुरगणाः प्रभवं न महर्षयः ।
अहमादिर्हि देवानां महर्षीणां च सर्वशः ॥
sentences.tr:
na me viduḥ sura-gaṇāḥ prabhavam na mahā-ṛṣayaḥ |
aham ādiḥ hi devānām mahā-ṛṣīṇām ca sarvaśaḥ ||

I (me: gen. sg. enclitic 'my', governing prabhavam)
to know (viduḥ: perfect 3rd pl. 'they know')
god, deity (first compound member)
host, multitude (sura-gaṇa: 'the hosts of gods', nom. pl. masc., subject)
origin, source, coming-into-being (acc. sg. masc., object of viduḥ)
not
great (first compound member)
sage, seer (mahā-ṛṣi: 'great sage', nom. pl. masc., subject, understood with viduḥ prabhavam repeated; ā + ṛ → ar)
I (nom. sg., subject; joined before ā-, no change)
beginning, origin (ādiḥ: nom. sg. masc., predicate)
for, indeed (particle; ādiḥ + hi: -iḥ + h- → -ir h-)
god, deity (gen. pl., 'of the gods')
great (first compound member)
sage (mahā-ṛṣi: gen. pl., 'of the great sages'; ā + ṛ → ar)
and
wholly, in every respect, altogether (adverb)

sentences.l: Not my origin the-hosts-of-gods know, nor the-great-sages; I [am] the-origin indeed of-the-gods and-of-the-great-sages, in-every-way.
sentences.i: Neither the hosts of the gods know my origin, nor the great sages; for I am, in every respect, the origin of the gods and of the great sages.
sentences.n: A double negative parallel (na ... na) states that no one — not even gods or great sages — knows Kṛṣṇa's prabhava, 'origin, source', because he precedes them all (ahamādir hi, 'for I am the origin'); this opens the chapter's argument for his unoriginated nature, continued through verse 3. Sandhi: महर्षयः and महर्षीणां both pack mahā+ṛṣi (ā+ṛ→ar), a compound recurring often in this chapter; अहमादिर्हि packs aham+ādiḥ, joined, +hi (-iḥ+h-→-ir h-).

sentences.t:
यो मामजमनादिं च वेत्ति लोकमहेश्वरम् ।
असंमूढः स मर्त्येषु सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥
sentences.tr:
yaḥ mām ajam anādim ca vetti loka-mahā-īśvaram |
a-saṃmūḍhaḥ saḥ martyeṣu sarva-pāpaiḥ pramucyate ||

morph.gloss: who, which (yaḥ: nom. sg. masc. relative pronoun, subject of vetti; -aḥ before m- → -o)
I (mām: acc. sg. 'me', object of vetti; joined before a-, no change)
unborn (ajam: acc. sg. masc., in apposition to mām; joined before a-, no change)
without beginning, beginningless (anādim: acc. sg. masc., in apposition to mām)
and
to know (vetti: present 3rd sg. 'knows')
world (first compound member)
great (second member)
lord (loka-mahā-īśvara: 'the great lord of the world', acc. sg. masc., in apposition to mām; ā + ī → e)
to be deluded, confused (saṃmūḍha: past participle negated by a-, 'undeluded', nom. sg. masc., subject)

he, that one (nom. sg. masc., resumptive subject; the pronoun sa/eṣa loses its visarga to sa before any following consonant, an exception to the ordinary -aḥ sandhi rules seen elsewhere in this chapter)
mortal (loc. pl., 'among mortals')
all (first compound member)
sin, evil (sarva-pāpa: 'all sins', instr. pl., 'from all sins')
to release, free (pramucyate: passive present 3rd sg. 'is released')

sentences.l: Who me, the-unborn and-the-beginningless, knows, the-great-lord-of-the-world — undeluded he among-mortals, from-all-sins is-released.
sentences.i: He who knows me as unborn and without beginning, the great lord of the world — that man, undeluded among mortals, is freed from all sins.
sentences.n: A relative-correlative construction (yaḥ, 'who' ... saḥ, 'that one'), the standard Gītā pattern for stating a general rule: whoever truly knows Kṛṣṇa as aja, 'unborn', and anādi, 'beginningless' — the point just established in verse 2 — is thereby freed. Loka-mahā-īśvaram, 'the great lord of the world' (ā+ī→e), is in apposition to mām. Sandhi: यो is yaḥ, -aḥ before m- → -o. Note also that the pronoun saḥ ('he') in the second line loses its visarga to sa before the following consonant m-, not to -o as महर्षयः did in verse 2 — sa and eṣa are irregular this way before any consonant, unlike ordinary nouns and adjectives.

sentences.t:
बुद्धिर्ज्ञानमसंमोहः क्षमा सत्यं दमः शमः ।
सुखं दुःखं भवोऽभावो भयं चाभयमेव च ॥
sentences.tr:
buddhiḥ jñānam a-saṃmohaḥ kṣamā satyam damaḥ śamaḥ |
sukham duḥkham bhavaḥ abhāvaḥ bhayam ca abhayam eva ca ||

morph.gloss: intellect, understanding, the faculty of discernment (nom. sg. fem., subject, understood with the verb bhavanti of verse 5; -iḥ + j- → -ir j-)
knowledge (nom. sg. neut., subject; joined before a-, no change)
freedom from delusion, non-confusion (from sam-muh; nom. sg. masc., subject)
patience, forbearance (nom. sg. fem., subject)
truth, truthfulness (nom. sg. neut., subject)
self-restraint, control of the senses (nom. sg. masc., subject)
tranquility, calmness of mind (nom. sg. masc., subject)
happiness, pleasure (nom. sg. neut., subject)
pain, suffering (nom. sg. neut., subject)
coming-into-being, existence (nom. sg. masc., subject; -aḥ + a- → -o with avagraha)
non-existence, ceasing-to-be (nom. sg. masc., subject; its own -aḥ before the voiced bh- of bhayam → -o)
fear (nom. sg. neut., subject)
and (ca + abhayam: a + a → ā)
fearlessness (nom. sg. neut., subject; joined before e-, no change)
and
indeed, too (eva belongs with the preceding cābhayam; this final ca is the correlative closing 'both fear and fearlessness')

sentences.l: Intellect, knowledge, freedom-from-delusion, patience, truth, self-restraint, tranquility; happiness, pain, existence, non-existence, fear and-fearlessness-too, and—
sentences.i: Intellect, knowledge, freedom from delusion, patience, truth, self-control, tranquility; happiness, sorrow, coming-to-be, ceasing-to-be, fear and fearlessness too—
sentences.n: The first of two verses (continuing through verse 5's first line) listing the states of mind and being that arise from Kṛṣṇa alone; all these nominals are subjects of bhavanti, 'they arise', in verse 5's second line, and the sentence is only completed there. Each term is translated individually (none of these — buddhi, jñāna, saṃmoha, kṣamā, and so on — is on the small untranslated-terms list of dharma/yoga/brahman/guṇa/sāṃkhya). Sandhi: बुद्धिर्ज्ञानमसंमोहः packs buddhiḥ+jñānam (-iḥ+j-→-ir j-) + asaṃmohaḥ, joined; भवोऽभावो packs bhavaḥ+abhāvaḥ (avagraha), whose own visarga then becomes -o before the voiced bh- of bhayam; चाभयमेव packs ca+abhayam (a+a→ā) + eva, joined.

sentences.t:
अहिंसा समता तुष्टिस्तपो दानं यशोऽयशः ।
भवन्ति भावा भूतानां मत्त एव पृथग्विधाः ॥
sentences.tr:
ahiṃsā samatā tuṣṭiḥ tapaḥ dānam yaśaḥ ayaśaḥ |
bhavanti bhāvāḥ bhūtānām mattaḥ eva pṛthag-vidhāḥ ||

morph.gloss: non-violence, non-injury (nom. sg. fem., subject)
sameness, equanimity (nom. sg. fem., subject)
contentment, satisfaction (nom. sg. fem., subject; -iḥ + t- → -is t-, visarga before a voiceless consonant)
austerity, ascetic heat (nom. sg. neut., subject; -aḥ before d- → -o)
giving, generosity, gift (nom. sg. neut., subject)
fame, glory (nom. sg. neut., subject; -aḥ + a- → -o with avagraha)
ill fame, infamy (nom. sg. neut., subject)
to be, come to be, arise (present 3rd pl. 'they arise'; the predicate completing the list of subjects begun in verse 4)
state, disposition, quality (nom. pl. masc., subject, summing up the list of verses 4-5a; visarga dropped before the voiced bh- of bhūtānām, the ending here being -āḥ, not -aḥ)
being (gen. pl., 'of beings')
me (mattaḥ: ablative sg. 'from me', formed with the ablative suffix -tas; visarga dropped before the vowel e- of eva)
alone, indeed ('from me alone')
separately, variously (first compound member; -k + v- → -g v-, voicing)
kind, sort (pṛthag-vidha: 'of various/manifold kinds', nom. pl. masc., agreeing with bhāvāḥ)

sentences.l: Non-violence, equanimity, contentment, austerity, generosity, fame and-ill-fame; they-arise, [these] dispositions, of-beings, from-me alone, of-manifold-kinds.
sentences.i: Non-violence, equanimity, contentment, austerity, charity, fame and disgrace — these various dispositions of beings arise from me alone, each in its own form.
sentences.n: This completes the sentence begun at verse 4: bhavanti, 'they arise', is the verb governing every noun listed there and in this verse's first line, all of them bhāvāḥ, 'dispositions, states', of bhūtānām, 'of beings', which come pṛthag-vidhāḥ, 'in manifold forms', mattaḥ eva, 'from me alone' — Kṛṣṇa is the single source of every mental and existential state, both the exalted (buddhi, jñāna...) and its opposite (duḥkham, ayaśaḥ...). Sandhi: तुष्टिस्तपो packs tuṣṭiḥ+tapaḥ (-iḥ+t-→-is t-, a visarga before a voiceless stop keeps -s rather than voicing to -r), whose own -aḥ then becomes -o before the voiced d- of dānam; यशोऽयशः packs yaśaḥ+ayaśaḥ (avagraha); भावा is bhāvāḥ with its visarga dropped (not -o) before the voiced bh- of bhūtānām, the same -āḥ pattern noted at verses 2-3 for the long-ā plural.

sentences.t:
महर्षयः सप्त पूर्वे चत्वारो मनवस्तथा ।
मद्भावा मानसा जाता येषां लोक इमाः प्रजाः ॥
sentences.tr:
mahā-ṛṣayaḥ sapta pūrve catvāraḥ manavaḥ tathā |
mad-bhāvāḥ mānasāḥ jātāḥ yeṣām lokaḥ imāḥ prajāḥ ||

morph.gloss: great (first compound member)
sage, seer (mahā-ṛṣi: 'great sage', nom. pl. masc., subject; ā + ṛ → ar)
seven (numeral, nom. pl., agreeing with maharṣayaḥ)
former, prior, ancient (nom. pl. masc., agreeing with maharṣayaḥ, 'of old')
four (catvāraḥ: numeral, nom. pl. masc., agreeing with manavaḥ; -aḥ before m- → -o)
Manu, the primal ancestor and lawgiver of mankind (Hindu cosmology names several; the 'four' here are the Manus of the current and preceding aeons; manavaḥ: nom. pl., subject)
likewise, so too (manavaḥ + tathā: -aḥ + t- → -as t-)
me (stem form, first compound member)

nature, state of being (mad-bhāva: 'of my nature, sprung from me', nom. pl. masc., agreeing with maharṣayaḥ and manavaḥ; visarga dropped before the voiced m- of mānasāḥ, the ending here being -āḥ, not -aḥ)
mind-born, mental, of the mind (nom. pl. masc., agreeing with the same subjects; visarga dropped before the voiced j- of jātāḥ)
to be born (jāta: past participle 'born', nom. pl. masc.; visarga dropped before the voiced y- of yeṣām)
who, which (yeṣām: gen. pl. relative, 'of whom', referring to the sages and Manus)
the world (nom. sg. masc., in loose apposition with prajāḥ, 'these creatures of the world'; -aḥ + i- → -a i-, visarga simply dropping before a vowel other than a-)
this (imāḥ: nom. pl. fem., agreeing with prajāḥ)
offspring, creature, progeny (nom. pl. fem., subject/predicate)

sentences.l: The-great-sages, seven, ancient, four Manus likewise, of-my-nature, mind-born, born — of-whom [is] the-world['s], these, creatures.
sentences.i: The seven great sages of old, and the four Manus as well, share my nature and were born of my mind; from them come these creatures of the world.
sentences.n: Kṛṣṇa now names, as instances of the mad-bhāvāḥ, 'states sprung from me', just listed in verses 4-5, the maharṣayaḥ sapta, 'seven great sages' (the traditional saptarṣi), and the four Manus, primal ancestors of mankind, all mānasāḥ jātāḥ, 'born of [Kṛṣṇa's] mind' — from whom in turn all present creatures descend. Sandhi: चत्वारो is catvāraḥ, -aḥ before m- → -o; मनवस्तथा packs manavaḥ+tathā (-aḥ+t-→-as t-); मद्भावा, मानसा and जाता each show a visarga (-āḥ, long-ā plural) simply dropping before the following voiced consonant, without becoming -o, the pattern first seen at verse 2's पुरुषा-type forms; लोक is lokaḥ with its own -aḥ dropping before the vowel इ- of imāḥ.

sentences.t:
एतां विभूतिं योगं च मम यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः ।
सोऽविकम्पेन योगेन युज्यते नात्र संशयः ॥
sentences.tr:
etām vibhūtim yogam ca mama yaḥ vetti tattvataḥ |
saḥ avikampena yogena yujyate na atra saṃśayaḥ ||

morph.gloss: this (acc. sg. fem., agreeing with vibhūtim)
manifestation, extraordinary power, glory (acc. sg. fem., object of vetti)
yoga, kept untranslated (acc. sg. masc., second object of vetti)
and
I (mama: gen. sg. 'my', modifying vibhūtim and yogam)
who, which (yaḥ: nom. sg. masc. relative, subject of vetti; -aḥ before v- → -o)
to know (vetti: present 3rd sg. 'knows')
true nature, reality, essence (tattvataḥ: adverb 'truly, in reality', formed with the ablative adverbial suffix -tas)
he (saḥ: nom. sg. masc., subject; -aḥ + a- → -o with avagraha)
unwavering, untrembling (avikampena: instr. sg., agreeing with yogena)
yoga, kept untranslated (instr. sg., 'with [unwavering] yoga')
to yoke, join, unite (yujyate: passive present 3rd sg. 'is united')
not (na + atra: a + a → ā)
here, in this matter
doubt (nom. sg. masc., subject)

sentences.l: This manifestation and-yoga of-mine, who truly knows — he with-unwavering yoga is-united; no-doubt here.
sentences.i: Whoever truly knows this manifestation and yoga of mine is united with me in unwavering yoga — of this there is no doubt.
sentences.n: Vibhūti, 'manifestation, extraordinary power', names the chapter's subject directly for the first time (it recurs as the chapter's title-word and again at verse 40); yoga here is Kṛṣṇa's own creative power of self-manifestation, kept untranslated like the yoga of other chapters, though the sense shades toward 'miraculous power' rather than disciplined practice. Sandhi: यो is yaḥ, -aḥ before v- → -o; सोऽविकम्पेन packs saḥ+avikampena (avagraha); नात्र packs na+atra (a+a→ā).

sentences.t:
अहं सर्वस्य प्रभवो मत्तः सर्वं प्रवर्तते ।
इति मत्वा भजन्ते मां बुधा भावसमन्विताः ॥
sentences.tr:
aham sarvasya prabhavaḥ mattaḥ sarvam pravartate |
iti matvā bhajante mām budhāḥ bhāva-samanvitāḥ ||

morph.gloss: I (nom. sg., subject)
all, everything (gen. sg., 'of everything')
origin, source (nom. sg. masc., predicate; -aḥ before m- → -o)
me (mattaḥ: ablative sg. 'from me')
all, everything (nom. sg. neut., subject)
to proceed, come forth, evolve (pravartate: present middle 3rd sg.)
thus (closing the preceding statement)
to think, consider (matvā: gerund 'having considered, understanding [this]')
to worship, revere, share in (bhajante: present middle 3rd pl. 'they worship')
I (acc. sg. 'me', object of bhajante)
wise, learned (nom. pl. masc., subject; visarga dropped before the voiced bh- of bhāvasamanvitāḥ, the ending here being -āḥ, not -aḥ)
feeling, disposition, state of mind (first compound member)
endowed with, possessed of, imbued with (bhāva-samanvita: 'endowed with [right] feeling', nom. pl. masc., agreeing with budhāḥ)

sentences.l: I of-all [am] the-origin; from-me all proceeds — thus having-considered, worship me the-wise, endowed-with-feeling.
sentences.i: I am the source of all; from me everything proceeds. Understanding this, the wise, filled with devotion, worship me.
sentences.n: This states directly the claim verses 2-7 have been building toward: Kṛṣṇa is sarvasya prabhavaḥ, 'the origin of all', so that the wise (budhāḥ) who grasp this (iti matvā, 'having understood thus') respond with bhajana, 'devotional worship' — a term distinct from the jñāna, 'knowledge', of the preceding verses, marking the turn from cosmology to devotion continued through verse 11. Sandhi: प्रभवो is prabhavaḥ, -aḥ before m- → -o; बुधा is budhāḥ with its visarga dropped (not -o) before the voiced bh- of bhāva-samanvitāḥ, the same -āḥ pattern seen through this chapter.

sentences.t:
मच्चित्ता मद्गतप्राणा बोधयन्तः परस्परम् ।
कथयन्तश्च मां नित्यं तुष्यन्ति च रमन्ति च ॥
sentences.tr:
mac-cittāḥ mad-gata-prāṇāḥ bodhayantaḥ parasparam |
kathayantaḥ ca mām nityam tuṣyanti ca ramanti ca ||

morph.gloss: me (stem form, first compound member; mat + citta: -t + c- → -c c-, assimilation)
mind, thought (mac-citta: 'whose thoughts are on me', nom. pl. masc., subject; visarga dropped before the voiced m- of madgataprāṇāḥ, the ending here being -āḥ, not -aḥ)
me (stem form, first compound member; mat + gata: -t + g- → -d g-, voicing)
gone to, directed towards (second member)
life-breath, vital energy (mad-gata-prāṇa: 'whose vital energies are absorbed in me', nom. pl. masc., subject, in apposition to maccittāḥ; visarga dropped before the voiced b- of bodhayantaḥ)
to awaken, understand (causative bodhayanti, 'to enlighten, instruct'; bodhayant: present participle, nom. pl. masc., 'instructing, enlightening [one another]')
each other, one another (parasparam: acc. sg., used adverbially, 'mutually')
to tell, relate, speak of (causative kathayati; kathayant: present participle, nom. pl. masc., 'speaking of [me]'; -aḥ + c- → -aś c-)
and
I (acc. sg. 'me', object of bodhayantaḥ and kathayantaḥ)
always, constantly (adverb)
to be content, satisfied (present 3rd pl.)
and
to delight, rejoice, take pleasure (present 3rd pl.)
and

sentences.l: With-minds-on-me, with-life-breaths-absorbed-in-me, enlightening one-another, and-speaking-of [me] constantly, [they are] content and they-delight.
sentences.i: With their minds fixed on me, their very life-breath absorbed in me, they enlighten one another and constantly speak of me; they find contentment and take delight.
sentences.n: This begins the chapter's portrait of the bhaktas, Kṛṣṇa's devotees (continued through verse 11), described first through two bahuvrīhi compounds, mac-cittāḥ and mad-gata-prāṇāḥ ('whose minds/life-breath are on me'), then through the mutual community of devotion — bodhayantaḥ parasparam, 'enlightening each other' — an ideal picture of satsaṅga, the company of the like-minded. Sandhi: मच्चित्ता packs mat+cittāḥ (-t+c-→-cc-), its own visarga then dropping before the voiced m- of madgataprāṇāḥ; मद्गतप्राणा packs mat+gata (-t+g-→-d g-) +prāṇāḥ, its visarga likewise dropping before the voiced b- of bodhayantaḥ; कथयन्तश्च is kathayantaḥ+ca (-aḥ+c-→-aś c-, the pattern already seen at 9.14's यतन्तश्च).

sentences.t:
तेषां सततयुक्तानां भजतां प्रीतिपूर्वकम् ।
ददामि बुद्धियोगं तं येन मामुपयान्ति ते ॥
sentences.tr:
teṣām satata-yuktānām bhajatām prīti-pūrvakam |
dadāmi buddhi-yogam tam yena mām upayānti te ||

morph.gloss: they, those (teṣām: gen. pl., 'of them', referring to the devotees of verse 9)
constant, continual (first compound member)
joined, disciplined, engaged (satata-yukta: 'constantly disciplined', gen. pl., agreeing with teṣām)
to worship, revere (bhajat: present participle 'worshiping', gen. pl., agreeing with teṣām)
love, affection (first compound member)
preceded by, accompanied by (prīti-pūrvakam: acc. sg. neut. used adverbially, 'lovingly, with affection')
to give (dadāmi: present 1st sg. 'I give')
intellect, understanding, the faculty of discernment (first compound member)
yoga, kept untranslated (buddhi-yoga: 'the yoga of understanding', acc. sg. masc., object of dadāmi)
that (acc. sg. masc., agreeing with buddhiyogam)
which (yena: instr. sg., 'by which')
I (mām: acc. sg. 'me', object of upayānti; joined before u-, no change)
to approach, come to (upayānti: present 3rd pl. 'they come to, attain')
they (nom. pl., resuming teṣām of pāda a)

sentences.l: To-them, constantly-disciplined, worshiping, lovingly, I-give the-yoga-of-understanding, that, by-which to-me they-come, they.
sentences.i: To them, ever disciplined, who worship me with love, I give the yoga of understanding by which they come to me.
sentences.n: This answers verse 9's portrait of the devotee with Kṛṣṇa's own promise: buddhi-yogam, 'the yoga of understanding' (or 'discriminative wisdom', cf. its earlier sense at 2.49 and 3.3; buddhi itself is translated, yoga kept untranslated), is given as a gift (dadāmi, 'I give') to those who worship prīti-pūrvakam, 'with love'. Sandhi: मामुपयान्ति packs mām+upayānti, joined, with no phonetic change since mām ends in the consonant -m.

sentences.t:
तेषामेवानुकम्पार्थमहमज्ञानजं तमः ।
नाशयाम्यात्मभावस्थो ज्ञानदीपेन भास्वता ॥
sentences.tr:
teṣām eva anukampā-artham aham ajñāna-jam tamaḥ |
nāśayāmi ātma-bhāva-sthaḥ jñāna-dīpena bhāsvatā ||

morph.gloss: they (teṣām: gen. sg., 'for them', referring to the devotees of verses 9-10; joined before e-, no change)
indeed, alone (eva + anukampā: a + a → ā)
compassion, sympathy (first compound member)
purpose, sake (anukampā-artham: acc. sg. neut. used adverbially, 'for the sake of compassion', 'out of compassion'; joined before a-, no change)
I (nom. sg., subject of nāśayāmi; joined before a-, no change)
ignorance, absence of knowledge (first compound member)
born, arising from (ajñāna-ja: 'born of ignorance', acc. sg. neut., agreeing with tamaḥ)
darkness (acc. sg. neut., object of nāśayāmi in the next line)
to be destroyed, perish (causative nāśayati, 'to destroy'; nāśayāmi: present 1st sg. 'I destroy'; -i + ā- → -y ā-)
self, soul (first compound member)
being, inner state (second member)
situated, abiding (ātma-bhāva-stha: 'abiding in [their] inmost being', nom. sg. masc., agreeing with the subject aham; -aḥ before j- → -o)
knowledge (first compound member)
lamp, light (jñāna-dīpa: 'the lamp of knowledge', instr. sg., instrumental means of destroying tamaḥ)
shining, radiant, brilliant (instr. sg., agreeing with jñānadīpena)

sentences.l: Of-them alone, out-of-compassion, I, ignorance-born darkness — abiding-in-their-being, I-destroy, with-the-lamp-of-knowledge, radiant.
sentences.i: Out of compassion for them alone, I, abiding within their being, destroy with the radiant lamp of knowledge the darkness born of ignorance.
sentences.n: Kṛṣṇa completes the promise of verse 10: the buddhi-yoga given to the devotees works by destroying (nāśayāmi) their ajñāna-jam tamaḥ, 'the darkness born of ignorance', from within — ātma-bhāva-sthaḥ, 'abiding in their [inner] being' — with the jñāna-dīpena bhāsvatā, 'radiant lamp of knowledge'. The whole first line is one long run of words joined purely by -m before a following vowel, with no phonetic change at any boundary. Sandhi: नाशयाम्यात्मभावस्थो packs nāśayāmi+ātma-bhāva-sthaḥ (-i+ā-→-y ā-), whose own -aḥ then becomes -o before the voiced j- of jñānadīpena.

sentences.t: अर्जुन उवाच
sentences.tr: arjuna uvāca
sentences.l: Arjuna said

morph.gloss: Arjuna, the third Pāṇḍava, the great archer (nom. sg.)
to speak (uvāca: perfect 3rd sg. 'said')

sentences.t:
परं ब्रह्म परं धाम पवित्रं परमं भवान् ।
पुरुषं शाश्वतं दिव्यमादिदेवमजं विभुम् ॥
sentences.tr:
param brahma param dhāma pavitram paramam bhavān |
puruṣam śāśvatam divyam ādi-devam ajam vibhum ||

morph.gloss: higher, supreme (nom. sg. neut., agreeing with brahma)
brahman, kept untranslated (nom. sg. neut., predicate to bhavān)
higher, supreme (nom. sg. neut., agreeing with dhāma)
abode, dwelling-place, radiance (nom. sg. neut., predicate to bhavān)
pure, purifying (nom. sg. neut., predicate to bhavān)
supreme, highest (nom. sg. neut., agreeing with pavitram, '[the] supreme [purifier]')
you, your reverence (bhavān: honorific 2nd person pronoun, nom. sg. masc., subject)
person, spirit (acc. sg. masc.; this line's epithets continue as object complements of āhuḥ tvām, 'they call you', in the next verse)
eternal, everlasting, perpetual (acc. sg. masc., agreeing with puruṣam)
divine, heavenly (acc. sg. masc., agreeing with puruṣam; joined before ā-, no change)
first, primal (first compound member)
god (ādi-deva: 'the primal god', acc. sg. masc., agreeing with puruṣam; joined before a-, no change)
unborn (ajam: acc. sg. masc., agreeing with puruṣam)
all-pervading, mighty, powerful (acc. sg. masc., agreeing with puruṣam)

sentences.l: The-supreme brahman, the-supreme abode, the-pure, the-supreme, [are] you; the-person, eternal, divine, the-primal-god, unborn, all-pervading —
sentences.i: You are the supreme brahman, the supreme abode, the pure, the supreme; the eternal, divine Person, the primal god, unborn, all-pervading —
sentences.n: Arjuna's great eulogy of Kṛṣṇa begins here, one long sentence spanning verses 12-13. This verse's first line is complete in itself: bhavān, 'you' (honorific), is said to be paraṃ brahma, 'the supreme brahman' (kept untranslated), and paraṃ dhāma, 'the supreme abode' — neuter nominal predicates used of the addressee, fitting for praise of the Absolute. The second line shifts to accusative forms (puruṣam, śāśvatam...) that are not governed by anything in this verse: they become the object complements of āhus tvām, 'they call you', which opens verse 13, so the two verses form a single sentence — a construction flagged here rather than repeated at verse 13. No sandhi splits words within this verse; दिव्यमादिदेवमजं simply strings three words together with -m written joined before each following vowel, with no phonetic change.

sentences.t:
आहुस्त्वामृषयः सर्वे देवर्षिर्नारदस्तथा ।
असितो देवलो व्यासः स्वयं चैव ब्रवीषि मे ॥
sentences.tr:
āhuḥ tvām ṛṣayaḥ sarve devarṣiḥ Nāradaḥ tathā |
Asitaḥ Devalaḥ Vyāsaḥ svayam ca eva bravīṣi me ||

morph.gloss: to say, declare, call (āhuḥ: perfect 3rd pl. 'they call'; -uḥ + t- → -us t-)
you (tvām: acc. sg., object of āhuḥ, continuing the epithets of verse 12 line b)
sage, seer (ṛṣayaḥ: nom. pl., subject of āhuḥ; joined before ṛ-, no change)
all (nom. pl. masc., agreeing with ṛṣayaḥ)
god, divine (first compound member)
sage (deva-ṛṣi: 'divine sage', a class of celestial seer, nom. sg. masc.; a + ṛ → ar)
the sage Nārada, a celestial seer and messenger among the gods, traditionally a son of Brahmā (nom. sg., in apposition to devarṣiḥ; -iḥ + n- → -ir n-)
likewise, also (Nāradaḥ + tathā: -aḥ + t- → -as t-)
the sage Asita, a seer associated with Devala (nom. sg.; -aḥ before d- → -o)
the sage Devala, often paired with Asita in tradition (nom. sg.; -aḥ before v- → -o)
the sage Vyāsa, compiler of the Vedas and the Mahābhārata, traditionally the poem's own narrator's source (nom. sg.)
oneself, in person (adverb/pronoun, here agreeing with the understood 'you')
and (ca + eva: a + e → ai)
indeed, also
to say, speak, declare (bravīṣi: present 2nd sg. 'you say')
I (me: dat. sg. enclitic 'to me')

sentences.l: [You] the-sages all call, the-divine-sage Nārada likewise; Asita, Devala, Vyāsa, and-yourself indeed you-declare to-me.
sentences.i: All the sages call you so, as does the divine sage Nārada; so do Asita, Devala and Vyāsa — and you yourself tell me so.
sentences.n: This completes the sentence begun in verse 12: āhuḥ tvām, 'they call you', governs all the accusative epithets of verse 12's second line; the list of authorities continues with devarṣiḥ Nāradaḥ ('the divine sage Nārada', a celestial seer and messenger of the gods), Asita and Devala (sages traditionally paired together), and Vyāsa (the sage credited with compiling the Vedas and composing the Mahābhārata itself), closing with Kṛṣṇa's own testimony, svayaṃ caiva bravīṣi me, 'and you yourself tell me so'. Sandhi: आहुस्त्वामृषयः packs āhuḥ+tvām (-uḥ+t-→-us t-) +ṛṣayaḥ, joined; देवर्षिर्नारदस्तथा packs deva+ṛṣiḥ (a+ṛ→ar) +Nāradaḥ (-iḥ+n-→-ir n-) +tathā (-aḥ+t-→-as t-); असितो and देवलो both show -aḥ before a voiced consonant → -o; चैव is ca+eva (a+e→ai).

sentences.t:
सर्वमेतदृतं मन्ये यन्मां वदसि केशव ।
न हि ते भगवन्व्यक्तिं विदुर्देवा न दानवाः ॥
sentences.tr:
sarvam etat ṛtam manye yat mām vadasi keśava |
na hi te bhagavan vyaktim viduḥ devāḥ na dānavāḥ ||

morph.gloss: all, entirely (sarvam: acc. sg. neut. used adverbially, 'wholly'; joined before e-, no change)
this (etat: acc. sg. neut., agreeing with ṛtam; -t + ṛ- → -d ṛ-, voicing before a vowel)
true, truth (acc. sg. neut., object of manye)
to think, believe, consider (manye: present middle 1st sg. 'I believe')
which (yat: acc. sg. neut. relative, referring to etad ṛtam, object of vadasi; -t + m- → -n m-, assimilation)
I (mām: acc. sg. 'me', object of vadasi)
to speak, say, tell (vadasi: present 2nd sg. 'you tell')
'having fine hair' or 'slayer of the demon Keśin', an epithet of Kṛṣṇa (vocative)
not
for, indeed (particle)
you (te: gen. sg. enclitic 'your', governing vyaktim)
the Blessed One, the Lord (bhagavan: vocative sg., addressing Kṛṣṇa; joined before v-, no change)
manifestation, self-revelation, true nature (vyaktim: acc. sg. fem., object of viduḥ)
to know (viduḥ: perfect 3rd pl. 'they know'; -uḥ + d- → -ur d-)
god, deity (devāḥ: nom. pl. masc., subject; visarga dropped before the voiced n- of na, the ending here being -āḥ, not -aḥ)
not, nor
demon, titan, son of Danu (nom. pl. masc., subject)

sentences.l: All this true I-believe, which to-me you-tell, O-slayer-of-Keśin; for not your, O-Lord, manifestation know the-gods, nor the-demons.
sentences.i: I believe all this to be true, Keśava, which you tell me; for, O Lord, neither the gods nor the demons know your true manifestation.
sentences.n: Arjuna closes his eulogy by affirming as ṛtam, 'true', everything Kṛṣṇa has told him, then adds his own observation: not even the gods or the dānavāḥ, 'demons, titans', know Kṛṣṇa's vyaktim, 'manifestation, true nature' — the very term the chapter's remaining verses go on to unfold. Keśava and bhagavan both address Kṛṣṇa directly. Sandhi: सर्वमेतदृतं packs sarvam+etat (joined) +ṛtam (-t+ṛ-→-d ṛ-); यन्मां is yat+mām (-t+m-→-n m-); विदुर्देवा packs viduḥ+devāḥ (-uḥ+d-→-ur d-), whose own visarga then drops before the voiced n- of na.

sentences.t:
स्वयमेवात्मनात्मानं वेत्थ त्वं पुरुषोत्तम ।
भूतभावन भूतेश देवदेव जगत्पते ॥
sentences.tr:
svayam eva ātmanā ātmānam vettha tvam puruṣa-uttama |
bhūta-bhāvana bhūta-īśa deva-deva jagat-pate ||

morph.gloss: oneself, of one's own accord (adverb)
indeed, emphatic (particle; eva + ātmanā: a + ā → ā)
self (ātmanā: instr. sg., 'by [your] own self')
self (ātmānam: acc. sg., 'your own self', object of vettha; ātmanā + ātmānam: ā + ā → ā)
to know (vettha: an old perfect form used as present, 2nd sg. 'you know')
you (nom. sg., subject)
person, spirit (first compound member)
highest, supreme (puruṣa-uttama: 'supreme Person', vocative sg., addressing Kṛṣṇa; a + u → o)
being, creature (first compound member)
one who brings into being, originator (from bhū causative; bhūta-bhāvana: 'origin of beings', vocative sg.)
being, creature (first compound member)
lord, ruler (bhūta-īśa: 'lord of beings', vocative sg.; a + ī → e)
god, deity (first compound member)
god, deity (deva-deva: 'god of gods', vocative sg.)
world, universe (first compound member)
lord, master (jagat-pate: 'lord of the world', vocative sg.)

sentences.l: By-yourself indeed with-your-own-self your-own-self you-know, you, O-supreme-person, O-origin-of-beings, O-lord-of-beings, O-god-of-gods, O-lord-of-the-world.
sentences.i: You alone truly know yourself, by yourself, O supreme Person, source of beings, lord of beings, god of gods, lord of the world.
sentences.n: Arjuna opens the second half of his eulogy (through v.18) by observing that only Kṛṣṇa can know himself, since he precedes and exceeds all other knowers — the reflexive svayam eva ātmanā ātmānam, 'you yourself, by your own self, [know] your own self', piles up the same pronoun three times for emphasis. The four vocatives that follow are all epithets of Kṛṣṇa: puruṣottama, 'supreme Person' (recalling puruṣam at 10.12); bhūtabhāvana, 'originator of beings' (bhāvana, causative of bhū); bhūteśa, 'lord of beings'; devadeva, 'god of gods'; jagatpate, 'lord of the world'. Sandhi: स्वयमेवात्मनात्मानं packs eva+ātmanā (a+ā→ā) and ātmanā+ātmānam (ā+ā→ā, no visible change since both are already long); भूतेश packs bhūta+īśa (a+ī→e).

sentences.t:
वक्तुमर्हस्यशेषेण दिव्या ह्यात्मविभूतयः ।
याभिर्विभूतिभिर्लोकानिमांस्त्वं व्याप्य तिष्ठसि ॥
sentences.tr:
vaktum arhasi aśeṣeṇa divyāḥ hi ātma-vibhūtayaḥ |
yābhiḥ vibhūtibhiḥ lokān imān tvam vyāpya tiṣṭhasi ||

morph.gloss: to speak (vaktum: infinitive, 'to declare, tell'; joined before a-, no change)
to deserve, be worthy, ought (arhasi: present 2nd sg., 'you should, ought to')

without remainder, in full (aśeṣeṇa: instr. sg. neut. used adverbially, 'exhaustively, fully'; arhasi + aśeṣeṇa: -i + a- → -ya, the glide-formation rule seen at 10.11 (-i + ā- → -yā) here extended to a following short a)
divine, heavenly (nom. pl. fem., agreeing with vibhūtayaḥ; visarga dropped before the voiced h- of hi, the -āḥ pattern seen since 10.2)
for, indeed (particle; hi + ātma-: -i + ā- → -y ā-, as at 10.11)
self, one's own (first compound member)
manifestation, extraordinary power (ātma-vibhūti: 'self-manifestation', nom. pl. fem., subject; cf. vibhūti at 10.7)
which (yābhiḥ: instr. pl. fem., 'by which')
manifestation (vibhūtibhiḥ: instr. pl., 'by [which] manifestations'; yābhiḥ + vibhūtibhiḥ: -iḥ + v- → -ir v-)
world (lokān: acc. pl. masc., object of vyāpya; vibhūtibhiḥ + lokān: -iḥ + l- → -ir l-)
this (imān: acc. pl. masc., agreeing with lokān; joined before i-, no change)
you (nom. sg., subject of tiṣṭhasi; imān + tvam: -n + t- → -ṃs t-, a new pattern — word-final -n before t-/th- inserts -s-)
to pervade, fill (vyāpya: gerund, 'having pervaded')
to stand, abide, remain (tiṣṭhasi: present 2nd sg., 'you stand, abide')

sentences.l: To-declare you-ought, without-remainder, [your] divine indeed self-manifestations; by-which manifestations these worlds you, having-pervaded, abide.
sentences.i: You should declare in full your divine manifestations, by which you pervade and abide in these worlds.
sentences.n: aśeṣeṇa, 'without remainder, exhaustively', qualifies vaktum arhasi, 'you ought to declare'; ātma-vibhūtayaḥ, 'your own manifestations', takes up the chapter's title-word vibhūti (cf. v.7) and turns it toward the catalog about to follow; the relative clause yābhiḥ...vyāpya tiṣṭhasi, 'by which...you pervade and abide', likewise anticipates that list. Sandhi: वक्तुमर्हस्यशेषेण packs vaktum+arhasi (joined) + aśeṣeṇa (-i+a-→-ya, the glide-formation already seen at 10.11 before ā, here before short a); दिव्या is divyāḥ with visarga dropped before the voiced h- of hi (the -āḥ pattern recurring since 10.2); ह्यात्मविभूतयः packs hi+ātma-vibhūtayaḥ (-i+ā-→-y ā-, as at 10.11); याभिर्विभूतिभिर् packs yābhiḥ+vibhūtibhiḥ (-iḥ+v-→-ir v-); लोकानिमांस्त्वं packs lokān+imān (joined) +tvam (-n+t-→-ṃs t-, a new pattern: word-final -n before t-/th- inserts -s-, giving -ṃs t-).

sentences.t:
कथं विद्यामहं योगिंस्त्वां सदा परिचिन्तयन् ।
केषु केषु च भावेषु चिन्त्योऽसि भगवन्मया ॥
sentences.tr:
katham vidyām aham yogin tvām sadā paricintayan |
keṣu keṣu ca bhāveṣu cintyaḥ asi bhagavan mayā ||

morph.gloss: how (interrogative adverb)
to know (vidyām: optative 1st sg., 'may I know'; joined before a-, no change)
I (nom. sg., subject)
one possessed of yoga, a yogin (vocative sg., addressing Kṛṣṇa)
you (tvām: acc. sg., object of paricintayan; yogin + tvām: -n + t- → -ṃs t-, as at 10.16)
always, constantly (adverb)
to reflect on, meditate upon (paricintayan: present participle, nom. sg. masc., 'meditating')
what, which (keṣu: loc. pl., 'in which')
what, which (keṣu: loc. pl., repeated for distributive sense, 'in each and every')
and
state of being, condition (loc. pl., 'in [what] states')
to think of, meditate on (cintyaḥ: gerundive, 'to be meditated upon', nom. sg. masc.; cintyaḥ + asi: -aḥ + a- → -o-)
to be (asi: present 2nd sg., 'you are')
the Blessed One, the Lord (bhagavan: vocative sg., addressing Kṛṣṇa; joined before m-, no change)
I (mayā: instr. sg., 'by me')

sentences.l: How may-I-know I, O-yogin, you, always meditating; in-which, in-which and states are-you-to-be-meditated-on, O-lord, by-me?
sentences.i: How may I know you, master of yoga, always meditating on you? And in which states of being am I to contemplate you, my Lord?
sentences.n: vidyām, an optative ('may I know'), governs the whole question; yogin addresses Kṛṣṇa as master of yoga; keṣu keṣu, 'in which, in which', a reduplication distributing over bhāveṣu, 'states of being' — 'in each of the various states'; cintyaḥ asi, gerundive plus copula, 'you are to be meditated upon'. Sandhi: योगिंस्त्वां packs yogin+tvām (-n+t-→-ṃs t-, as at 10.16); चिन्त्योऽसि packs cintyaḥ+asi (-aḥ+a-→-o-, avagraha, as at 10.4, 10.5, 10.7).

sentences.t:
विस्तरेणात्मनो योगं विभूतिं च जनार्दन ।
भूयः कथय तृप्तिर्हि शृण्वतो नास्ति मेऽमृतम् ॥
sentences.tr:
vistareṇa ātmanaḥ yogam vibhūtim ca janārdana |
bhūyaḥ kathaya tṛptiḥ hi śṛṇvataḥ na asti me 'mṛtam ||

morph.gloss: extent, detail, length (vistareṇa: instr. sg. used adverbially, 'at length, in full detail')
self (ātmanaḥ: gen. sg., 'of your own'; vistareṇa + ātmanaḥ: a + ā → ā, its own visarga then becoming -o before the voiced y- of yogam)
yoga, kept untranslated (acc. sg., object of kathaya)
manifestation (acc. sg., object of kathaya; cf. 10.7, 10.16)
and
'rouser' or 'tormentor of men', an epithet of Kṛṣṇa (vocative sg.)
again, once more (adverb; cf. 10.1)
to tell, relate (causative; kathaya: imperative 2nd sg., 'speak! declare!')
satisfaction, satiety (nom. sg. fem., subject of asti; tṛptiḥ + hi: -iḥ + h- → -ir h-, as at 10.13's devarṣir nāradas)
for, indeed (particle)
to hear (śṛṇvataḥ: present participle, gen. sg. masc., 'of [me] hearing, listening'; -aḥ before n- → -o)
not (na + asti: a + a → ā)
to be, exist (asti: present 3rd sg., 'there is')
I (me: gen. sg. enclitic 'my, for me')
nectar of immortality (amṛtam: nom. sg. neut., subject of asti, 'this nectar'; me + amṛtam: avagraha, lost a- restored)

sentences.l: At-length your-own yoga and-manifestation, O-rouser-of-men; again speak — satiety indeed of-[me]-listening there-is-not, for-me, [this] nectar.
sentences.i: Tell me again in full detail, Janārdana, of your yoga and your manifestation; for I never tire of hearing this nectar.
sentences.n: Arjuna's fourfold question (vv.15-18) closes by asking Kṛṣṇa to speak bhūyaḥ, 'again', and vistareṇa, 'at length' — the very fullness he had already asked for with aśeṣeṇa at v.16 — since the amṛtam, 'nectar', of this teaching never satisfies him (tṛptiḥ...na asti, 'there is no satiety'). Janārdana, 'rouser' or 'tormentor of men', is an epithet of Kṛṣṇa. Sandhi: विस्तरेणात्मनो packs vistareṇa+ātmanaḥ (a+ā→ā), whose own visarga becomes -o before the voiced y- of yogam; तृप्तिर्हि packs tṛptiḥ+hi (-iḥ+h-→-ir h-, the same voicing seen in devarṣir nāradas at 10.13); शृण्वतो is śṛṇvataḥ, -aḥ before n- → -o; नास्ति packs na+asti (a+a→ā); मेऽमृतम् packs me+amṛtam (avagraha).

sentences.t: श्रीभगवानुवाच
sentences.tr: śrībhagavān uvāca
sentences.l: The Blessed Lord said

morph.gloss: holy, glorious (honorific prefix)
the Blessed One, the Lord — Kṛṣṇa's title as speaker (nom. sg. bhagavān; -n + u- written joined)
to speak (uvāca: perfect 3rd sg. 'said')

sentences.t:
हन्त ते कथयिष्यामि दिव्या ह्यात्मविभूतयः ।
प्राधान्यतः कुरुश्रेष्ठ नास्त्यन्तो विस्तरस्य मे ॥
sentences.tr:
hanta te kathayiṣyāmi divyāḥ hi ātma-vibhūtayaḥ |
prādhānyataḥ kuru-śreṣṭha na asti antaḥ vistarasya me ||

morph.gloss: well then! come now! (interjection)
you (te: dat. sg. enclitic, 'to you')
to tell, declare (causative; kathayiṣyāmi: future 1st sg., 'I will declare')
divine, heavenly (nom. pl. fem., agreeing with vibhūtayaḥ; visarga dropped before the voiced h- of hi, as at 10.16)
for, indeed (particle; hi + ātma-: -i + ā- → -y ā-, as at 10.11, 10.16)
self, one's own (first compound member)
manifestation (ātma-vibhūti: 'self-manifestation', nom. pl. fem., object of kathayiṣyāmi; cf. 10.16)
chiefness, primacy, being foremost (prādhānyataḥ: ablative-formed adverb, 'chiefly, in the main')
the Kuru clan, Arjuna's own lineage (first compound member)
best, foremost (kuru-śreṣṭha: 'best of the Kurus', vocative sg., addressing Arjuna)
not (na + asti: a + a → ā)
to be, exist (asti: present 3rd sg.; asti + antaḥ: -i + a- → -y a-, as at 10.16's arhasyaśeṣeṇa)
end, limit (antaḥ: nom. sg. masc., subject; -aḥ before v- → -o)
extent, detail (gen. sg., 'of [my] extent')
I (me: gen. sg. enclitic 'my')

sentences.l: Well-then, to-you I-will-declare [my] divine indeed self-manifestations, chiefly, O-best-of-the-Kurus; there-is-no-end of-my extent.
sentences.i: Very well, Kuruśreṣṭha — I will declare to you my divine manifestations, but only the chief ones; there is no end to my extent.
sentences.n: Kṛṣṇa answers Arjuna's fourfold question (vv.15-18) and opens the great catalog of vibhūtis that runs to v.42; prādhānyataḥ, 'by way of the chief ones', concedes that only the principal manifestations can be told, since — as the second line states, and as v.40 will state again — his vistara, 'extent', has no end. Kuruśreṣṭha, 'best of the Kurus', addresses Arjuna. Sandhi: दिव्या and ह्यात्मविभूतयः repeat 10.16's pattern; नास्त्यन्तो packs na+asti (a+a→ā) +antaḥ (-i+a-→-ya, as at 10.16), whose own visarga becomes -o before the voiced v- of vistarasya.

sentences.t:
अहमात्मा गुडाकेश सर्वभूताशयस्थितः ।
अहमादिश्च मध्यं च भूतानामन्त एव च ॥
sentences.tr:
aham ātmā guḍākeśa sarva-bhūta-āśaya-sthitaḥ |
aham ādiḥ ca madhyam ca bhūtānām antaḥ eva ca ||

morph.gloss: I (nom. sg., subject; joined before ā-, no change)
self, soul (ātmā: nom. sg., predicate, 'I am the Self')
'lord of sleep', an epithet of Arjuna for his mastery over drowsiness (vocative sg.)
all (first compound member)
being, creature (second member)
resting-place, seat, abode (bhūta-āśaya: 'the seat [heart] of beings'; a + ā → ā, third member)
situated, abiding (sarva-bhūta-āśaya-sthita: 'abiding in the heart of all beings', nom. sg. masc., agreeing with ātmā)
I (nom. sg., subject; joined before ā-, no change)
beginning (ādiḥ: nom. sg. masc., predicate; ādiḥ + ca: -iḥ + c- → -iś c-)
and
middle (nom. sg. neut., predicate)
and
being, creature (bhūtānām: gen. pl., 'of beings')
end (antaḥ: nom. sg. masc., predicate; visarga dropped before the vowel e- of eva, -aḥ + e- → -a e-, as at 10.1's bhūya eva)
indeed, truly (particle)
and

sentences.l: I [am] the-self, O-lord-of-sleep, seated-in-the-heart of-all-beings; I [am] the-beginning and the-middle and, of-beings, the-end too.
sentences.i: I am the Self, Guḍākeśa, seated in the heart of all beings; I am the beginning, the middle, and the end of beings as well.
sentences.n: This opens the catalog proper (through v.42): Kṛṣṇa first identifies himself with the universal ātman, 'Self', dwelling in every creature's āśaya, 'seat, heart', then states his cosmic completeness as beginning, middle and end of beings — a claim echoed again at v.32. Guḍākeśa, 'lord of sleep', is an epithet of Arjuna. Sandhi: सर्वभूताशयस्थितः packs bhūta+āśaya (a+ā→ā); अहमादिश्च packs aham+ādiḥ (joined) +ca (-iḥ+c-→-iś c-, as kathayantaś ca at 10.9); भूतानामन्त packs bhūtānām+antaḥ, its visarga dropping before the vowel e- of eva exactly as bhūyaḥ eva did at 10.1 (-aḥ + non-a vowel → -a, with no further merging of the resulting a with the following vowel).

sentences.t:
आदित्यानामहं विष्णुर्ज्योतिषां रविरंशुमान् ।
मरीचिर्मरुतामस्मि नक्षत्राणामहं शशी ॥
sentences.tr:
ādityānām aham viṣṇuḥ jyotiṣām raviḥ aṃśumān |
marīciḥ marutām asmi nakṣatrāṇām aham śaśī ||

morph.gloss: a class of twelve solar deities, sons of Aditi (ādityānām: gen. pl., 'of the Ādityas')
I (nom. sg., subject; joined before a-, no change)
the god Viṣṇu, here reckoned chief among the Ādityas (nom. sg., predicate; viṣṇuḥ + jyotiṣām: -uḥ + j- → -ur j-)
light, luminary (jyotiṣām: gen. pl., 'of lights')
the sun (nom. sg., predicate; raviḥ + aṃśumān: -iḥ + a- → -ir a-)
possessed of rays, radiant (aṃśumān: nom. sg. masc., agreeing with raviḥ, 'the radiant [sun]')
the sage Marīci, reckoned chief among the Maruts and elsewhere one of the seven great sages (cf. 10.6) (nom. sg., predicate; marīciḥ + marutām: -iḥ + m- → -ir m-)
the Maruts, storm- and wind-gods (marutām: gen. pl., 'of the Maruts')
to be (asmi: present 1st sg., 'I am'; joined before a-, no change)
lunar mansion, constellation (nakṣatrāṇām: gen. pl., 'of the constellations')
I (nom. sg., subject; joined before a-, no change)
the moon, 'the hare-marked one' (nom. sg., predicate)

sentences.l: Of-the-Ādityas I [am] Viṣṇu, of-lights the-sun, radiant; of-the-Maruts Marīci I-am, of-constellations I [am] the-moon.
sentences.i: Of the Ādityas I am Viṣṇu; of lights, the radiant sun; of the Maruts, Marīci; of the constellations, the moon.
sentences.n: The catalog's basic pattern appears here for the first time in its full form: a class named in the genitive plural, and Kṛṣṇa identified with its foremost member ('of X, I am Y'); the pattern recurs through v.42, growing terser as it repeats, and is not re-explained at each occurrence. The Ādityas are the twelve solar deities, sons of Aditi, among whom Viṣṇu is reckoned chief; the Maruts are the storm-gods, here led by the sage Marīci (elsewhere counted among the seven great sages, cf. 10.6). Sandhi: विष्णुर्ज्योतिषां and मरीचिर्मरुतामस्मि both voice a final -iḥ/-uḥ to -ir/-ur before a following voiced sound, the pattern recurring through this chapter (e.g. 10.13, 10.18); रविरंशुमान् likewise voices -iḥ to -ir before the vowel a-.

sentences.t:
वेदानां सामवेदोऽस्मि देवानामस्मि वासवः ।
इन्द्रियाणां मनश्चास्मि भूतानामस्मि चेतना ॥
sentences.tr:
vedānām sāmavedaḥ asmi devānām asmi vāsavaḥ |
indriyāṇām manaḥ ca asmi bhūtānām asmi cetanā ||

morph.gloss: the Veda (gen. pl., 'of the Vedas')
the Sāmaveda, the Veda of chants (nom. sg., predicate; sāmavedaḥ + asmi: -aḥ + a- → -o-)
god (devānām: gen. pl., 'of gods')
to be (asmi: present 1st sg.; joined before a-, no change)
'lord of the Vasus', a name of Indra, king of the gods (nom. sg., predicate)
sense-organ, faculty (gen. pl., 'of the senses')
mind (manaḥ: nom. sg., predicate; manaḥ + ca: -aḥ + c- → -aś c-)
and (ca + asmi: a + a → ā)
to be (asmi: present 1st sg.)
being, creature (bhūtānām: gen. pl., 'of beings')
to be (asmi: joined before a-, no change)
consciousness, sentience (nom. sg. fem., predicate)

sentences.l: Of-the-Vedas the-Sāmaveda I-am; of-gods I-am Vāsava; of-the-senses the-mind and-I-am; of-beings I-am consciousness.
sentences.i: Of the Vedas I am the Sāmaveda; of the gods, Vāsava (Indra); of the senses, the mind; of beings, consciousness.
sentences.n: Vāsava, 'lord of the Vasus', is a name of Indra, king of the gods. Sandhi: सामवेदोऽस्मि packs sāmavedaḥ+asmi (-aḥ+a-→-o-, avagraha, as at 10.17); मनश्चास्मि packs manaḥ+ca (-aḥ+c-→-aś c-) +asmi (a+a→ā).

sentences.t:
रुद्राणां शंकरश्चास्मि वित्तेशो यक्षरक्षसाम् ।
वसूनां पावकश्चास्मि मेरुः शिखरिणामहम् ॥
sentences.tr:
rudrāṇām śaṅkaraḥ ca asmi vitteśaḥ yakṣa-rakṣasām |
vasūnām pāvakaḥ ca asmi meruḥ śikhariṇām aham ||

morph.gloss: Rudra, a class of storm-gods presided over by Śiva (gen. pl., 'of the Rudras')
'beneficent one', a name of Śiva (nom. sg., predicate; śaṅkaraḥ + ca: -aḥ + c- → -aś c-)
and (ca + asmi: a + a → ā)
to be (asmi: present 1st sg.)
wealth, property (first compound member)
lord (vitta-īśa: 'lord of wealth', a name of Kubera, nom. sg., predicate; a + ī → e, its own visarga becoming -o before the voiced y- of yakṣarakṣasām)
a class of demigod, a nature-spirit (first compound member)
a class of demon (yakṣa-rakṣas: gen. pl., 'of yakṣas and rākṣasas')
a class of eight deities, the Vasus (gen. pl., 'of the Vasus')
'purifier', a name of Agni, the fire-god (nom. sg., predicate; pāvakaḥ + ca: -aḥ + c- → -aś c-)
and (ca + asmi: a + a → ā)
to be (asmi: present 1st sg.)
the cosmic mountain Meru, at the center of the world (nom. sg., predicate)
having a peak, a peaked mountain (gen. pl., 'of peaked mountains')
I (nom. sg., subject; joined before a-, no change)

sentences.l: Of-the-Rudras Śaṅkara and-I-am, the-lord-of-wealth of-yakṣas-and-rākṣasas; of-the-Vasus Pāvaka and-I-am, Meru of-peaked-mountains I.
sentences.i: Of the Rudras I am Śaṅkara (Śiva); of yakṣas and rākṣasas, the lord of wealth (Kubera); of the Vasus, Pāvaka (Agni); of the peaked mountains, Meru.
sentences.n: Śaṅkara is a name of Śiva, head of the eleven Rudras; Vitteśa, 'lord of wealth', names Kubera, treasurer of the gods and overlord of yakṣas and rākṣasas; Pāvaka, 'purifier', is a name of Agni, chief of the eight Vasus; Meru is the cosmic mountain at the world's axis. Sandhi: शंकरश्चास्मि and पावकश्चास्मि both pack -aḥ+ca (-aḥ+c-→-aś c-) +asmi (a+a→ā), as at v.22; वित्तेशो packs vitta+īśa (a+ī→e), its visarga becoming -o before the voiced y- of yakṣarakṣasām.

sentences.t:
पुरोधसां च मुख्यं मां विद्धि पार्थ बृहस्पतिम् ।
सेनानीनामहं स्कन्दः सरसामस्मि सागरः ॥
sentences.tr:
purodhasām ca mukhyam mām viddhi pārtha bṛhaspatim |
senānīnām aham skandaḥ sarasām asmi sāgaraḥ ||

morph.gloss: household priest, chaplain (gen. pl., 'of household priests')
and
chief, foremost (acc. sg. masc., agreeing with mām, object complement)
I (acc. sg. 'me', object of viddhi)
to know (viddhi: imperative 2nd sg., 'know!')
'son of Pṛthā', an epithet of Arjuna (vocative sg.)
the preceptor and chief priest of the gods (acc. sg., in apposition to mām, 'me — Bṛhaspati')
army-leader, commander (gen. pl., 'of army-commanders')
I (nom. sg., subject; joined before a-, no change)
the war-god Skanda (Kārttikeya), commander of the gods' armies (nom. sg., predicate)
lake, pool, body of water (sarasām: gen. pl., 'of bodies of water')
to be (asmi: present 1st sg.; joined before a-, no change)
the ocean (nom. sg., predicate)

sentences.l: Of-household-priests and the-chief me know, O-son-of-Pṛthā, Bṛhaspati; of-army-commanders I [am] Skanda, of-bodies-of-water I-am the-ocean.
sentences.i: And know me to be Bṛhaspati, chief of household priests, Pārtha; of army commanders I am Skanda; of lakes I am the ocean.
sentences.n: Bṛhaspati, preceptor and chief priest of the gods, is here named foremost among purodhasaḥ, 'household priests'; Skanda (Kārttikeya) leads the gods' armies as senānī. Pārtha, 'son of Pṛthā [Kuntī]', addresses Arjuna. No sandhi splits any word in this verse; each token is simply written joined before its following vowel with no phonetic change (senānīnām+aham, sarasām+asmi).

sentences.t:
महर्षीणां भृगुरहं गिरामस्म्येकमक्षरम् ।
यज्ञानां जपयज्ञोऽस्मि स्थावराणां हिमालयः ॥
sentences.tr:
maharṣīṇām bhṛguḥ aham girām asmi ekam akṣaram |
yajñānām japa-yajñaḥ asmi sthāvarāṇām himālayaḥ ||

morph.gloss: great (first compound member; mahā + ṛṣi: ā + ṛ → ar, as at 10.2, 10.6, 10.13)
sage (mahā-ṛṣi: gen. pl., 'of the great sages')
the great sage Bhṛgu, one of the mind-born sons of Brahmā (nom. sg., predicate; bhṛguḥ + aham: -uḥ + a- → -ur a-)
I (nom. sg., subject; bhṛguḥ + aham: -uḥ + a- → -ur a-)
speech, utterance, word (girām: gen. pl., 'of utterances')
to be (asmi: present 1st sg.; asmi + ekam: -i + e- → -y e-)
one, single (first compound member; joined before a-, no change)
imperishable, syllable (eka-akṣara: 'the single syllable', i.e. the sacred Oṃ, acc. sg. neut., predicate)
sacrifice (gen. pl., 'of sacrifices')
muttered prayer, silent repetition (first compound member)
sacrifice (japa-yajña: 'the sacrifice of silent recitation', nom. sg., predicate; japayajñaḥ + asmi: -aḥ + a- → -o-)
stationary, immovable (gen. pl., 'of immovable things')
'abode of snow', the Himālaya mountains (nom. sg., predicate)

sentences.l: Of-the-great-sages Bhṛgu I; of-utterances I-am the-single syllable; of-sacrifices the-sacrifice-of-silent-repetition I-am, of-immovable-things the-Himālaya.
sentences.i: Of the great sages I am Bhṛgu; of utterances, the single syllable Oṃ; of sacrifices, the sacrifice of silent recitation; of immovable things, the Himālaya.
sentences.n: Bhṛgu, one of the seven great sages (mahaṛṣi), a group referenced generally at 10.6; the 'single syllable' (ekam akṣaram) is the sacred Oṃ, held to be the essence of all speech; japa-yajña, 'the sacrifice of silently repeating [a mantra]', is ranked here above outward ritual sacrifice. Sandhi: महर्षीणां packs mahā+ṛṣīṇām (ā+ṛ→ar, as before); भृगुरहं shows -uḥ+a-→-ur a-; गिरामस्म्येकमक्षरम् packs girām+asmi (joined) +ekam (-i+e-→-y e-, the same glide mechanism as -i+a-/-i+ā- at 10.11 and 10.16, here before e-) +akṣaram (joined); जपयज्ञोऽस्मि packs japayajñaḥ+asmi (-aḥ+a-→-o-, avagraha).

sentences.t:
अश्वत्थः सर्ववृक्षाणां देवर्षीणां च नारदः ।
गन्धर्वाणां चित्ररथः सिद्धानां कपिलो मुनिः ॥
sentences.tr:
aśvatthaḥ sarva-vṛkṣāṇām deva-ṛṣīṇām ca nāradaḥ |
gandharvāṇām citrarathaḥ siddhānām kapilaḥ muniḥ ||

morph.gloss: the sacred fig tree, Ficus religiosa (nom. sg., predicate)
all (first compound member)
tree (sarva-vṛkṣa: gen. pl., 'of all trees')
god (first compound member; deva + ṛṣi: a + ṛ → ar, as at 10.13)
sage (deva-ṛṣi: gen. pl., 'of divine sages')
and
the celestial sage Nārada, already named at 10.13 (nom. sg., predicate)
a class of celestial musician (gen. pl., 'of gandharvas')
'having a bright chariot', king of the gandharvas (nom. sg., predicate)
a class of semi-divine being possessed of supernatural powers (gen. pl., 'of siddhas')
the sage Kapila, traditionally the founder of the Sāṃkhya system (nom. sg., predicate; -aḥ before m- → -o)
sage (nom. sg., in apposition to Kapilaḥ)

sentences.l: The-sacred-fig-tree, of-all-trees; and-of-divine-sages, Nārada; of-gandharvas, Citraratha; of-siddhas, the-sage Kapila.
sentences.i: Of all trees I am the sacred fig; of divine sages, Nārada; of gandharvas, Citraratha; of siddhas, the sage Kapila.
sentences.n: Nārada, the celestial sage and divine messenger, already named among Kṛṣṇa's witnesses at 10.13; Citraratha is traditionally king of the gandharvas, the celestial musicians; the siddhas are perfected beings of supernatural power, among whom Kapila — traditionally credited as founder of the Sāṃkhya system (cf. 2.39) — is named foremost. Sandhi: देवर्षीणां packs deva+ṛṣīṇām (a+ṛ→ar); कपिलो shows -aḥ before m- → -o, as elsewhere in this chapter.

sentences.t:
उच्चैःश्रवसमश्वानां विद्धि माममृतोद्भवम् ।
ऐरावतं गजेन्द्राणां नराणां च नराधिपम् ॥
sentences.tr:
uccaiḥśravasam aśvānām viddhi mām amṛta-udbhavam |
airāvatam gaja-indrāṇām narāṇām ca nara-adhipam ||

morph.gloss: 'long-eared' or 'loud-neighing', the divine horse that arose at the churning of the ocean of milk (uccaiḥśravasam: acc. sg., object of viddhi; joined before a-, no change)
horse (aśvānām: gen. pl., 'of horses')
to know (viddhi: imperative 2nd sg., 'know!')
I (mām: acc. sg. 'me', object of viddhi, in apposition to Uccaiḥśravasam; joined before a-, no change)
the nectar of immortality (first compound member)
arisen, sprung from (amṛta-udbhava: 'sprung from the nectar of immortality', acc. sg. masc., agreeing with Uccaiḥśravasam, alluding to the churning of the ocean of milk; a + u → o)
the divine elephant of Indra, likewise born at the churning of the ocean (acc. sg., in apposition to mām)
elephant (first compound member; gaja + indra: a + i → e)
lord, chief (gaja-indra: 'lordly elephant', gen. pl., 'of lordly elephants')
man (gen. pl., 'of men')
and
man (first compound member; nara+adhipa: a+a→ā)
lord, ruler (nara-adhipa: 'the lord of men, the king', acc. sg., in apposition to mām)

sentences.l: Uccaiḥśravas, of-horses, know me, arisen-from-the-nectar-of-immortality; Airāvata, of-lordly-elephants, of-men and the-king.
sentences.i: Know me, of horses, to be Uccaiḥśravas, sprung from the nectar of immortality; of lordly elephants, Airāvata; and of men, the king.
sentences.n: Uccaiḥśravas, the divine horse, and Airāvata, Indra's elephant, both arose from the amṛta-manthana, the churning of the ocean of milk by gods and demons for the nectar of immortality — the myth the epithet amṛtodbhavam, 'sprung from the nectar', recalls. Sandhi: उच्चैःश्रवसमश्वानां and माममृतोद्भवम् both show final -m simply written joined before a following vowel with no phonetic change; within the latter, amṛta+udbhavam shows a+u→o; गजेन्द्राणां packs gaja+indrāṇām (a+i→e); नराधिपम् packs nara+adhipam (joined, no change).

sentences.t:
आयुधानामहं वज्रं धेनूनामस्मि कामधुक् ।
प्रजनश्चास्मि कन्दर्पः सर्पाणामस्मि वासुकिः ॥
sentences.tr:
āyudhānām aham vajram dhenūnām asmi kāmadhuk |
prajanaḥ ca asmi kandarpaḥ sarpāṇām asmi vāsukiḥ ||

to be (asmi: present 1st sg.; joined before a-, no change)
'yielding [every] desire', the wish-fulfilling cow Kāmadhenu (nom. sg., predicate)

to be (asmi: present 1st sg.)
the god of love, Kāma (nom. sg., in apposition to prajanaḥ)

to be (asmi: present 1st sg.; joined before a-, no change)
Vāsuki, king of the serpents (nom. sg., predicate)

sentences.l: Of-weapons I [am] the-thunderbolt, of-cows I-am the-wish-fulfilling-cow; the-progenitor and-I-am, Kandarpa; of-serpents I-am Vāsuki.
sentences.i: Of weapons I am the thunderbolt; of cows, the wish-fulfilling cow (Kāmadhenu); I am the progenitor, Kandarpa (the god of love); of serpents, Vāsuki.
sentences.n: Kāmadhuk, 'yielding every desire', names Kāmadhenu, the wish-fulfilling cow born — like Uccaiḥśravas and Airāvata in the previous verse — at the churning of the ocean; Kandarpa is another name of Kāma, the god of love, here called prajanaḥ, 'the begetter', as the personified desire that generates all beings; Vāsuki is the great serpent-king. Sandhi: प्रजनश्चास्मि packs prajanaḥ+ca (-aḥ+c-→-aś c-) +asmi (a+a→ā), as at vv.22-23.

sentences.t:
अनन्तश्चास्मि नागानां वरुणो यादसामहम् ।
पितॄणामर्यमा चास्मि यमः संयमतामहम् ॥
sentences.tr:
anantaḥ ca asmi nāgānām varuṇaḥ yādasām aham |
pitṝṇām aryamā ca asmi yamaḥ saṃyamatām aham ||

I (nom. sg., subject; joined before a-, no change)
ancestor, forefather (pitṝṇām: gen. pl., 'of ancestors')
Aryaman, one of the Ādityas, presiding over ancestors and the sacred order (nom. sg., predicate; joined before a-, no change)
and (ca + asmi: a + a → ā)
to be (asmi: present 1st sg.)
Yama, god of death and lord of the ancestors, restrainer of all beings by law (nom. sg., predicate)
to restrain, control (saṃyamatām: present participle gen. pl., 'of those who restrain, administer law')
I (nom. sg., subject; joined before a-, no change)

sentences.l: Ananta and-I-am, of-nāgas; Varuṇa, of-water-deities, I; of-ancestors Aryaman and-I-am, Yama, of-restrainers, I.
sentences.i: Of the nāgas I am Ananta; of water-deities, Varuṇa; of ancestors, Aryaman; of those who administer law, Yama.
sentences.n: Ananta is Śeṣa, the cosmic serpent-king on whom Viṣṇu reclines between cycles of creation, here named chief among nāgas, the serpent-deities; Varuṇa presides over the waters and yādāṃsi, water-creatures; Aryaman, one of the twelve Ādityas, is associated with ancestors and the sacred order; Yama, god of death, is named foremost among saṃyamatām, 'those who restrain, administer law'. Sandhi: अनन्तश्चास्मि and चास्मि both pack -aḥ+c-→-aś c- and/or ca+asmi (a+a→ā), as regularly since v.22; वरुणो shows -aḥ before y- → -o.

sentences.t:
प्रह्लादश्चास्मि दैत्यानां कालः कलयतामहम् ।
मृगाणां च मृगेन्द्रोऽहं वैनतेयश्च पक्षिणाम् ॥
sentences.tr:
prahlādaḥ ca asmi daityānām kālaḥ kalayatām aham |
mṛgāṇām ca mṛga-indraḥ aham vainateyaḥ ca pakṣiṇām ||

sentences.i: Of the daityas I am Prahlāda; of calculators, Time; of beasts, the lion; and of birds, Vainateya (Garuḍa).
sentences.n: Prahlāda, the devout daitya king rescued by Viṣṇu's Narasiṃha incarnation from his demon father Hiraṇyakaśipu, is named chief of the daityas, just as at v.23 Śiva was named chief of the Rudras; kālaḥ, 'Time', recurs from the famous 11.32 (kept capitalized here as there, the house rendering); mṛgendra, 'lord of beasts', is the lion; Vainateya, 'son of Vinatā', is Garuḍa, king of the birds and Viṣṇu's mount. Sandhi: प्रह्लादश्चास्मि and वैनतेयश्च both pack -aḥ+c-→-aś c-; मृगेन्द्रोऽहं packs the compound mṛga+indra (a+i→e) then mṛgendraḥ+aham (-aḥ+a-→-o-, avagraha).

sentences.t:
पवनः पवतामस्मि रामः शस्त्रभृतामहम् ।
झषाणां मकरश्चास्मि स्रोतसामस्मि जाह्नवी ॥
sentences.tr:
pavanaḥ pavatām asmi rāmaḥ śastra-bhṛtām aham |
jhaṣāṇām makaraḥ ca asmi srotasām asmi jāhnavī ||

to be (asmi: present 1st sg.; joined before a-, no change)

weapon (first compound member)

I (nom. sg., subject; joined before a-, no change)
fish, sea-creature (gen. pl., 'of fish')
the crocodile, a mythical river-monster (nom. sg., predicate; makaraḥ + ca: -aḥ + c- → -aś c-)
and (ca + asmi: a + a → ā)
to be (asmi: present 1st sg.)

sentences.l: The-wind, of-purifiers, I-am; Rāma, of-weapon-bearers, I; of-fish and the-crocodile-I-am, of-rivers I-am Jāhnavī.
sentences.i: Of purifiers I am the wind; of weapon-bearers, Rāma; of fish, the crocodile; and of rivers, the Gaṅgā.
sentences.n: pavana, 'wind', is named foremost among pavatām, 'purifying things'; Rāma is ambiguous — commentators read it as either Paraśurāma, the axe-wielding warrior-brāhmaṇa and sixth avatāra of Viṣṇu, or Rāmacandra, hero of the Rāmāyaṇa and seventh avatāra, and the verse gives no way to decide between them. makara, translated here as 'the crocodile', is a mythical river-monster, sometimes pictured as crocodile-like; Jāhnavī, 'daughter of Jahnu' (the sage said to have once swallowed and then released the river), is a name of the Gaṅgā (Ganges). Sandhi: मकरश्चास्मि packs -aḥ+c-→-aś c- + a+a→ā, as regularly.

sentences.t:
सर्गाणामादिरन्तश्च मध्यं चैवाहमर्जुन ।
अध्यात्मविद्या विद्यानां वादः प्रवदतामहम् ॥
sentences.tr:
sargāṇām ādiḥ antaḥ ca madhyam ca eva aham arjuna |
adhyātma-vidyā vidyānām vādaḥ pravadatām aham ||

beginning (ādiḥ: nom. sg. masc., predicate; sargāṇām + ādiḥ: joined, no change; ādiḥ + antaḥ: -iḥ + a- → -ir a-)

and

I (nom. sg., subject; joined before a-, no change)
Arjuna (vocative)

adhyātma, 'pertaining to the self' (glossed here as svabhāva, one's own essential nature); the fixed English rendering, set at 8.3's review, is 'the individual self' (first compound member; i + ā → y ā, the same glide-formation as -i + ā- at 10.11, 10.16, here compound-internally)

science, branch of knowledge (gen. pl., 'of sciences')

to speak forth, argue, debate (pravadatām: present participle gen. pl., 'of debaters, disputants')

sentences.l: Of-creations the-beginning and-the-end, and the-middle indeed, I-am, Arjuna; of-sciences the-science-of-the-individual-self, of-debaters the-debate, I.
sentences.i: Of creations I am the beginning, the end, and the middle too, Arjuna; of sciences, the science of the individual self; of debaters, the argument.
sentences.n: sarga, 'creation, emanation', restates of every act of creation the beginning-middle-end claim already made at v.20; adhyātma-vidyā, 'the science of the self' in the verse's own gloss — adhyātma, 'pertaining to the self', whose fixed English rendering (set at 8.3's review) is 'the individual self' — is named foremost among vidyā, 'branches of knowledge'; vāda, 'reasoned argument, debate', is likewise claimed among pravadatām, 'debaters, disputants'. Sandhi: सर्गाणामादिरन्तश्च packs sargāṇām+ādiḥ (joined, no change) +antaḥ (-iḥ+a-→-ir a-) +ca (-aḥ+c-→-aś c-); चैवाहमर्जुन packs ca+eva (a+e→ai) +aham (a+a→ā) +arjuna (joined, no change); अध्यात्मविद्या packs adhi+ātman (i+ā→y ā, the same glide formation as -i+ā- at 10.11, 10.16, here compound-internally).

sentences.t:
अक्षराणामकारोऽस्मि द्वन्द्वः सामासिकस्य च ।
अहमेवाक्षयः कालो धाताहं विश्वतोमुखः ॥
sentences.tr:
akṣarāṇām akāraḥ asmi dvandvaḥ sāmāsikasya ca |
aham eva akṣayaḥ kālaḥ dhātā aham viśvataḥ-mukhaḥ ||

the copulative compound (dvandva), a Sanskrit grammatical term for compounds whose members are coordinated as if joined by 'and' (nom. sg., predicate)
belonging to a compound, compound-word (adj. used substantively, gen. sg. as a class-genitive, 'of compound words')
and

imperishable, undecaying (nom. sg., predicate, agreeing with kālaḥ)
Time (nom. sg., predicate, in apposition to akṣayaḥ; -aḥ before dh- → -o)
ordainer, creator, establisher (dhātā: nom. sg. masc., predicate; ā + a → ā)

sentences.l: Of-letters the-[syllable]-A I-am, the-copulative-compound of-compounds and; I-alone imperishable Time, the-ordainer-I facing-every-direction.
sentences.i: Of letters I am the letter A; and of compounds, the copulative compound; I alone am imperishable Time; I am the ordainer, facing every direction.
sentences.n: akāra, the syllable A, is held to be the seed of all speech, as Oṃ was at v.25; the copulative compound — dvandva, the 'pair' compound (e.g. Rāma-Lakṣmaṇau, 'Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa') — is named foremost among sāmāsika, 'compound words', a piece of Sanskrit grammatical terminology; akṣayaḥ kālaḥ, 'imperishable Time', echoes the kālaḥ of v.30 and the famous kālaḥ of 11.32 (the house rendering kept here too); dhātṛ, 'ordainer, creator', with viśvatas-mukhaḥ, 'facing every direction', recalls the four-faced creator Brahmā of tradition, here claimed by Kṛṣṇa himself. Sandhi: अक्षराणामकारोऽस्मि packs -aḥ+a-→-o- (avagraha), as regularly; अहमेवाक्षयः packs eva+akṣayaḥ (a+a→ā); कालो shows -aḥ before dh-→-o; धाताहं shows ā+a→ā (dhātā+aham); विश्वतोमुखः is a compound whose internal visarga voices to -o before the consonant m-, as with kapilaḥ muniḥ at 10.26.

sentences.t:
मृत्युः सर्वहरश्चाहमुद्भवश्च भविष्यताम् ।
कीर्तिः श्रीर्वाक्च नारीणां स्मृतिर्मेधा धृतिः क्षमा ॥
sentences.tr:
mṛtyuḥ sarva-haraḥ ca aham udbhavaḥ ca bhaviṣyatām |
kīrtiḥ śrīḥ vāk ca nārīṇām smṛtiḥ medhā dhṛtiḥ kṣamā ||

and
woman; feminine being (gen. pl., marking the seven nouns of this verse as the class of famous feminine qualities personified as goddesses)

sentences.l: Death, the-all-seizer-and-I-am, and-the-origin, of-things-to-come; Fame, Fortune-and-Speech, of-feminine[-things], Memory, Intelligence, Firmness, Patience.
sentences.i: I am death, the all-seizer, and the origin of things to come; and, among feminine qualities, fame, fortune, speech, memory, intelligence, firmness, and patience.
sentences.n: sarva-haraḥ, 'seizer of all', names death as the universal taker; udbhava, 'arising', paired with bhaviṣyatām, 'of things to come', names Kṛṣṇa as the source, the rising prosperity, of what is yet to be. The list that follows names seven famous feminine-gender nouns — kīrti (fame), śrī (fortune, beauty), vāk (speech), smṛti (memory), medhā (intelligence), dhṛti (steadfastness), kṣamā (patience) — traditionally personified as goddesses, all identified with Kṛṣṇa under the marker nārīṇām, 'of feminine [qualities]'. Sandhi: सर्वहरश्चाहमुद्भवश्च packs sarvaharaḥ+ca (-aḥ+c-→-aś c-) +aham (a+a→ā; joined before u-, no change) +udbhavaḥ+ca (-aḥ+c-→-aś c-); श्रीर्वाक्च packs śrīḥ+vāk (-īḥ+v-→-īr v-, the same -iḥ/-īḥ voicing pattern as elsewhere, here on a long vowel); स्मृतिर्मेधा packs smṛtiḥ+medhā (-iḥ+m-→-ir m-).

sentences.i: Of hymns I am, thus, the Bṛhatsāman; of metres, the Gāyatrī; of months, Mārgaśīrṣa; of seasons, the flower-bearer (spring).
sentences.n: the Bṛhatsāman is a celebrated Sāmavedic melody; the Gāyatrī, most sacred of Vedic metres, is the metre of the famous Gāyatrī mantra; Mārgaśīrṣa (November–December) is reckoned the first and most auspicious month of the traditional calendar; kusumākara, 'the flower-abundance', personifies spring, the season of flowering.
